Earlier this year in March, Apple announced it would discontinue the Mac Pro and confirmed there were no plans to release a new generation of Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg today published a new report providing additional background on Apple's Mac Pro strategy, revealing an unexpected detail about a product Apple once developed...

The Inside Story on Apple's Shelved Mac Pro Plans

In the latest issue of his "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman explains that "abandoning the Mac Pro" was "not always the plan" inside Apple. Gurman reiterates a point from previous reporting: Apple originally intended to release a chip called "Extreme," positioned above its "Ultra" chips.

The report states: "Apple is said to have developed both an M2 Extreme and an M3 Extreme chip, but ultimately cancelled the project due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific hardware of the Mac Pro that was once in development, Gurman says Apple had two models (with the internal codenames J170 and J190) in the works, but they never made it to market.

Perhaps the most intriguing detail in this report is that one of those models used an Intel processor:

Apple ultimately discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its website, and directed buyers to the Mac Studio instead. Although signs had long pointed to this day eventually arriving, for supporters of Mac Pro hardware, it still marks the quiet end of an era.

What are your thoughts on Apple's decision to shut down the Mac Pro product line rather than continue the "Extreme" chip roadmap into the Apple Silicon era? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
